alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb.

One substantive rendered by fine flour. Head placed on flour under rule 31's tie clause, the ASV writing flour as an ordinary class noun with fine as the specifier; the competing reading treats flour as a supplied generic and heads on fine, as dry land does.
Finite verb to bake, sharing the auxiliary written for the earlier verb.
Definite direct-object marker with no English of its own; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).
Object suffix rendered thereof (rule 18); the pronoun stands after the object noun, which rule 25 allows.
Two-and-ten rendered by the single word twelve fuses under rule 30; neither morpheme owns a part of the word, so the first token is the deterministic anchor.
One substantive rendered tenth parts; the generic parts joins the unit under rule 31 and the head stays on tenth, which carries the lexeme, since part alone is any part.

The italic of an ephah supplies both the function word and the measure noun the Hebrew never writes, which is rule 33's added case — the same as the italic reeds after five and twenty thousand — rather than rule 31's completion of a substantive's lexeme. Subtraction decides it: dropping the phrase leaves no Hebrew noun short of a relation it bears, and what goes is a noun the Hebrew does not write. The italics corroborate without deciding (rule 7). The competing reading folds the phrase into עֶשְׂרֹנִים as an unpacking of that word's lexical of an ephah, on the model of sea monsters.
The ASV writes no the for the phrase; the determiner it does write is the numeral's own one (rules 29, 41).
Agreement article on the numeral; the phrase carries no written the (rules 29, 47).
Numeral with the supplied in that rule 33 gives an adverbial nominal, placed on the word the preposition stands before; the competing reading puts in on the noun חַלָּה as the phrase's head noun.

review_notes: Corrected: the italic of an ephah is split off as its own added unit. It supplies a preposition, an article and a measure noun in a clause whose Hebrew names none of them, which is exactly rule 33's added case and the reeds precedent; the accepted alignment folded it into עֶשְׂרֹנִים under rule 31 while itself calling it a supplied measure.
עֶשְׂרֹנִים keeps the supplied generic parts and heads on tenth under rule 31; only the measure phrase moved.
fine flour is headed on flour under rule 31's tie clause, with the competing reading recorded in that unit's note.
The supplied in of in one cake is placed under rule 33 on the word it stands before in the English; putting it on חַלָּה is the defensible alternative and is named in that unit's note.
